newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen condemns Turkish security buffer plan.
newsitem.headline: Yemen condemns Turkish security buffer plan.

text.p: Yemen on Monday condemned Turkey's plans to set up a security buffer zone in Kurdish northern Iraq, the official Saba news agency reported.
It quoted a foreign ministry official as saying the move violated the sovereignty of Iraq and that Yemen viewed it as "a threat to Arab and Turkish relations."
Yemen's condemnation was part of a chorus of Arab criticism of the plan. The critics included states that backed the military campaign to drive Iraqi forces out of Kuwait in 1991.

Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, a pillar of Arab opposition to Iraqi President Saddam Hussein during the Kuwait crisis, said in remarks published on Monday that partitioning Iraq or annexing Iraqi territory would be grave.
Turkey has said the security zone, which would be temporary, is needed to prevent infiltration by separatist Kurdish rebels who have waged a 12-year-old insurgency in southeast Turkey.
